## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one animation tick (blink phase, `app.motion`), the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`, `ChangedMsg.Failures`), the activity-column guard (`activity_guard_test.go`), the terminal hand-off to child processes (the exec wrapper `internal/ui/teaexec`, use it instead of `tea.ExecProcess`, D121) and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci`, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface` |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage`, `internal/ui/datatable`, and the activity indicator column (`internal/ui/indicator`, `datatable.IndicatorColumn`, the row sentences `components.DescribeRow`) |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# Planning Rules

## Implementation Plans

- **Location**: Always write implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` in the current project directory.
- **Format**: Use Markdown format for plans.
- **Naming**: Use descriptive names like `feature-name-plan.md` or `YYYY-MM-DD-feature-name.md`.

## Antigravity IDE Integration

When using the Antigravity IDE extension:
- Save all implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` relative to the project root.
- Create the directory if it doesn't exist before saving plans.
- Plans should be accessible from both Claude Code CLI and Antigravity IDE.

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing

mise run cover        # Coverage per package
```

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

31	   - **Recommandation : A.** Aucune touche ni règle nouvelle, et c'est le sens de la fiche UX.
32	3. **Avertissement (« suspendus ou annulés »).** Le registre n'a **pas** d'état « suspendu » :
33	   un blur ne suspend aucun job (app-shell.md, DEVDESK-210). Il ne reste que l'annulation.
34	   - A. Avertissement tant qu'un run annulé n'est pas soldé : l'arrêt est demandé et le
35	     travail en vol est attendu (sync, clone, file en cours de vidage). Une fois soldé :
36	     `nil`.
37	   - B. A, plus les runs annulés soldés jusqu'à leur acquittement, comme pour les échecs.
38	   - **Recommandation : A.** L'utilisateur a lui-même demandé l'annulation (`K` dans `:jobs`,
39	     `esc` dans l'explorateur). Un jaune persistant après coup serait du bruit. Si une
40	     suspension apparaît un jour dans le registre, elle se branchera ici.
41	
42	## Faits techniques établis (Bubble Tea v2.1.1)
43	
44	- `tea.View.ProgressBar *tea.ProgressBar` porte `{State, Value}`. Les états sont `None`,
45	  `Default` (valeur 0 à 100), `Error`, `Indeterminate` et `Warning`. `tea.NewProgressBar`
46	  borne la valeur à [0, 100].
47	- Le renderer n'écrit OSC 9;4 que lorsque la valeur change. Il compare `*last != *view` **par
48	  valeur à travers le pointeur gardé**. **Piège :** muter en place un `*tea.ProgressBar` déjà
49	  rendu rend le changement invisible. `View()` doit donc fournir un pointeur neuf à chaque
50	  appel, ce que garantit une fonction pure qui fabrique la valeur.
51	- Premier rendu avec `nil` : rien n'est écrit. Passage de non-nil à nil : `ESC ]9;4;0 BEL`
52	  (`ansi.ResetProgressBar`).
53	- `close()` (sortie, panique récupérée, `ExecProcess`) écrit la remise à zéro si la dernière
54	  vue avait une barre. `start()` (retour d'un `ExecProcess`) la réémet. **Le critère 1 « à la
55	  sortie » est donc tenu par le framework**, et on l'épingle par un test sur les octets
56	  (étape 3).
57	- Il n'existe ni requête de capacité OSC 9;4, ni détection dans Bubble Tea : la séquence part
58	  vers tout terminal. Un parseur ECMA-48 consomme une chaîne OSC jusqu'à BEL ou ST sans
59	  l'imprimer. DevDesk envoie déjà OSC 11 et 111 ainsi que le mode 1004. Le cas réel « tmux
60	  sans passthrough » reste à vérifier à la main (étape 5).
61	
62	## Le total d'un lot est-il connu ? Oui : tout est livrable d'un coup
63	
64	`Run.Total()` et `Run.Done()` existent. `Done` compte les items soldés : done, skipped et
65	failed. Un run ouvert (`NewOpenRun`, le clone pendant le parcours) n'a pas de total tant
66	qu'il n'est pas scellé (`Seal`). Ensuite, il en a un. Le pourcentage est donc calculable
67	sans toucher au registre. Le découpage en étapes permet malgré tout de livrer d'abord
68	l'indéterminé, l'erreur et l'avertissement (étapes 1 et 2), puis de vérifier le pourcentage
69	sur Windows Terminal (étape 5).
70	
71	## Règles d'agrégation (à tester et à documenter)
72	
73	Entrée : les runs **non soldés** du périmètre et les échecs du périmètre. Précédence, de la
74	plus forte à la plus faible (même ordre que la Rule 128 : error, warning, status) :
75	
76	| # | Condition | `jobs.Progress.State` | `tea.ProgressBar` |
77	|---|---|---|---|
78	| 1 | ≥1 échec avec `Seq > readThrough` (non lu) | `ProgressError` | `{Error, 100}` |
79	| 2 | ≥1 run non soldé avec `Cancelled()` | `ProgressWarning` | `{Warning, Percent}` si mesuré, sinon `{Warning, 100}` |
80	| 3 | ≥1 run non soldé, tous mesurés | `ProgressPercent` | `{Default, Percent}` |
81	| 4 | ≥1 run non soldé, au moins un non mesuré | `ProgressIndeterminate` | `{Indeterminate, 0}` |
82	| 5 | sinon | `ProgressIdle` | `nil` |
83	
84	- **Run mesuré** : `!run.Open() && run.Total() >= 2`. *Hypothèse :* un run à une cible
85	  (scan d'un élément, create, delete, index, pull unitaire) n'a pas de progression utile :
86	  il resterait à 0 % puis disparaîtrait. Il compte donc comme indéterminé.
87	- **Pourcentage** : `floor(100 × Σ Done / Σ Total)` sur les runs non soldés, c'est-à-dire
88	  une somme pondérée et non la moyenne des pourcentages. Exemple : 1/2 et 0/8 donnent 10 %,
89	  pas 25 %. Le résultat est borné à [0, 100]. Un run seulement en file vaut 0 %.
90	- **Mixte** : un seul run non mesuré rend l'ensemble indéterminé (hypothèse du brief).
91	- **Un échec non lu domine tout**, y compris un registre vide (critère 4). Il disparaît
92	  aussi sans acquittement lorsque l'échec est effacé (nouvelle tentative réussie, `Forget`).
93	- *Hypothèse :* les valeurs 100 pour `Error` et pour `Warning` non mesuré donnent une barre
94	  pleine et visible sur Windows Terminal. À vérifier à la main (étape 5).
95	- *Hypothèse :* les échecs du kind `index` (parcours de la forge à l'ouverture de session)
96	  comptent, car `:jobs` les montre. Hors ligne, l'onglet passera au rouge jusqu'à la visite
97	  de `:jobs`. Choix ouvert, signalé dans la doc.
98	
99	## Étapes
100	
101	Dépendances : 1, puis 2, puis 3. L'étape 4 ne dépend que de la 1 et peut se mener en
102	parallèle des étapes 2 et 3. L'étape 5 vient en dernier.
103	
104	### Étape 1 : domaine (`internal/jobs`), numéro d'échec et fonction pure d'agrégation
105	
106	Fichiers : `internal/jobs/failure.go`, `internal/jobs/registry.go`, nouveau
107	`internal/jobs/progress.go`, nouveau `internal/jobs/progress_test.go`, et
108	`internal/jobs/registry_failure_test.go` (ajouts).
109	
110	Interfaces :
111	
112	```go
113	// failure.go: Failure gains a registry-assigned, strictly increasing number.
114	type Failure struct {
115		FailureKey
116		Display string
117		Detail  string
118		At      time.Time
119		// Seq orders failures for acknowledgement. Assigned by Registry.pose, never
120		// reused, strictly greater on every pose (a re-posed key gets a new Seq).
121		Seq uint64
122	}
123	
124	// LatestFailureSeq returns the highest Seq in failures, 0 when empty.
125	func LatestFailureSeq(failures []Failure) uint64
126	
127	// FailuresIn keeps the failures filed under contextName (D8, like FilterContext).
128	func FailuresIn(failures []Failure, contextName string) []Failure
129	
130	// registry.go: Registry gains `failureSeq uint64`; pose sets f.Seq = ++r.failureSeq.
131	
132	// progress.go
133	type ProgressState int
134	
135	const (
136		ProgressIdle ProgressState = iota
137		ProgressIndeterminate
138		ProgressPercent
139		ProgressWarning
140		ProgressError
141	)
142	
143	// Progress is the whole registry summarized for one reader: the terminal tab
144	// (router) and the :jobs footer read the same computation.
145	type Progress struct {
146		State    ProgressState
147		Percent  int  // 0..100, meaningful when Measured
148		Measured bool // every unfinished run is sealed with >= 2 targets
149		Running  int  // unfinished runs
150		Stopping int  // unfinished runs asked to stop (Run.Cancelled)
151		Unread   int  // failures with Seq > readThrough
152	}
153	
154	// Summarize applies the precedence table. runs and failures are already scoped
155	// by the caller (FilterContext / FailuresIn); it never filters by context.
156	func Summarize(runs []Run, failures []Failure, readThrough uint64) Progress
157	```
158	
159	Pourquoi `Seq` et non `At` : deux échecs peuvent porter le même horodatage (résolution de
160	l'horloge, `SetClock` en test). Un filigrane fondé sur le temps en perdrait un.
161	
162	Tests à écrire d'abord (tables, `progress_test.go`). Construire les runs avec `jobs.New()`
163	puis `Start`, `Advance`, `Cancel`, `Seal` et `Snapshot()`, ou par champs dans le package :
164	
165	| Entrée | Attendu |
166	|---|---|
167	| `nil, nil, 0` | `Progress{}` (Idle) |
168	| un run soldé `done` | Idle (critère 6) |
169	| run ouvert non scellé, 0 cible | Indeterminate, Running 1 |
170	| `NewImmediateRun` (1 cible, running) | Indeterminate (hypothèse 1 cible) |
171	| scellé 4 cibles : 1 done, 1 failed, 2 queued, échec déjà lu | Percent 50, Measured |
172	| 1/2 et 0/8 | Percent 10, pas 25 |
173	| 1/3 | Percent 33 (arrondi par défaut) |
174	| 3 cibles toutes queued | Percent 0, State Percent |
175	| mesuré et ouvert ensemble | Indeterminate |
176	| sync annulé, un item encore running | Warning, Stopping 1 ; Percent conservé si mesuré |
177	| run annulé soldé | Idle |
178	| échec `Seq 3`, readThrough 2 | Error, Unread 1 |
179	| échec `Seq 3`, readThrough 3 | pas Error |
180	| échec non lu et run running | Error (précédence) |
181	| échec non lu et run en arrêt | Error |
182	| aucun run, échec non lu | Error (critère 4) |
183	
184	Registre (`registry_failure_test.go`) :
185	
186	- chaque `pose` attribue un `Seq` strictement croissant ;
187	- un échec reposé sur la même clé reçoit un `Seq` plus grand que l'ancien ;
188	- `Failures()` transporte `Seq` ;
189	- après l'éviction au-delà de `MaxFailures`, aucun `Seq` n'est réutilisé ;
190	- `LatestFailureSeq(nil) == 0`, puis le maximum ;
191	- `FailuresIn` ne garde que le contexte demandé.
192	
193	Les littéraux `jobs.Failure{…}` existants des tests sont à champs nommés : ils compilent tels
194	quels, et aucune comparaison de struct entière n'a été trouvée.
195	
196	Critère de fin : `go test ./internal/jobs` est vert, et `go test -fuzz` n'est pas concerné.
197	
198	### Étape 2 : routeur, calcul, acquittement et affectation de `View.ProgressBar`
199	
200	Fichiers : nouveau `internal/app/terminal_progress.go`, `internal/app/app.go` (champs, appel
201	dans `Update`), `internal/app/jobs.go` (`broadcastJobs`), `internal/app/view.go` (seule
202	affectation), nouveau `internal/app/terminal_progress_test.go`,
203	`internal/app/terminal_background_test.go` (garde factorisé).
204	
205	Interfaces :
206	
207	```go
208	// terminal_progress.go
209	
210	// terminalProgress maps the summary to the tab's progress bar. Pure; returns a
211	// fresh pointer on every call (the renderer compares through the pointer it
212	// kept, so an in-place mutation would never be redrawn). nil when Idle.
213	func terminalProgress(p jobs.Progress) *tea.ProgressBar
214	
215	// summarizeJobs scopes the snapshot to msg.Context, acknowledges what :jobs
216	// shows when it is on screen, and stores the summary. Called from Update only.
217	func (a *App) summarizeJobs(msg jobs.ChangedMsg)
218	
219	// syncTerminalProgress is the level check run after every Update: it
220	// re-summarizes when the context changed since the last summary, or when :jobs
221	// is on screen with an unread failure (entry by any path: switchView,
222	// returnToOrigin, ...). Otherwise it does nothing (no snapshot copy per tick).
223	func (a *App) syncTerminalProgress()
224	```
225	
226	Champs d'`App` :
227	
228	```go
229	progress            jobs.Progress     // last summary; read by View()
230	progressContext     string            // context the summary was computed for
231	failuresReadThrough map[string]uint64 // acknowledgement watermark per context
232	```
233	
234	Un filigrane par contexte : avec un seul filigrane global, acquitter dans B marquerait comme
235	lus les échecs de A de `Seq` inférieur, jamais vus. Avec la réponse B à la question 1, un
236	filigrane unique suffit.
237	
238	Câblage :
239	
240	- `broadcastJobs` : `msg := a.changedMsg()` puis `a.summarizeJobs(msg)` avant la boucle. Le
241	  calcul part bien du snapshot `ChangedMsg` (critère 7). Toute écriture du registre passe par
242	  `jobsChanged`, donc par `broadcastJobs`.
243	- `summarizeJobs` : `runs := jobs.Unfinished(jobs.FilterContext(msg.Runs, msg.Context))` et
244	  `fails := jobs.FailuresIn(msg.Failures, msg.Context)`. Si
245	  `a.currentView == command.ViewJobs`, le filigrane du contexte passe à
246	  `LatestFailureSeq(fails)`. Ensuite `a.progress = jobs.Summarize(runs, fails, readThrough)`
247	  et `a.progressContext = msg.Context`.
248	- `App.Update` (wrapper) : `model, cmd := a.update(msg)`, puis `a.syncTerminalProgress()`,
249	  puis `ensureTick` comme aujourd'hui.
250	- `view.go` : `v.ProgressBar = terminalProgress(a.progress)`. C'est la seule affectation du
251	  dépôt, et `View()` reste sans effet de bord.
252	- Le blur ne touche pas la barre : l'onglet sert justement quand DevDesk n'a pas le focus.

255	
256	- mapping en table : Idle donne nil ; Indeterminate donne `{Indeterminate, 0}` ; Percent 42

258	  `{Warning, 100}` ; Error donne `{Error, 100}` ;
259	- deux appels donnent deux pointeurs distincts, et muter le premier ne change pas le second ;

262	  (`a.jobs.Advance` puis `a.jobsChanged()`) : `{Default, 50}`. Tout `done` : `nil`

264	- run ouvert (`NewOpenRun` clone) : Indeterminate. Après `Seal` avec 2 cibles dont 1 faite :

267	  `switchView(ViewJobs)` puis un `Update` : `nil`. Retour à `ws` : toujours `nil`. Un nouvel
268	  échec : de nouveau Error ;
269	- un échec arrivé pendant que `:jobs` est affiché ne passe jamais à Error ;
270	- avec la réponse A à la question 1 : un échec d'un run du contexte A, contexte courant B,
271	  ne donne pas Error. De retour dans A, Error. Acquitter dans B n'acquitte pas A ;
272	- `CancelMsg` sur un sync dont un item tourne : Warning. Item soldé : `nil` ;
273	- changement de contexte sans diffusion : la barre suit le nouveau contexte (`progressContext`) ;
274	- critère 8 : `a.View().Content` est identique avec `a.progress` renseigné ou remis à zéro.
275	  La barre ne touche que le champ `ProgressBar` ;
276	- garde source `TestOnlyTheRouterSetsTheTerminalProgress` : factoriser le corps de
277	  `TestOnlyTheRouterSetsTheTerminalBackground` en
278	  `assertOnlyOwnerSets(t *testing.T, owner, field string)` (Rule 201, pas de doublon) et
279	  l'appeler pour `BackgroundColor` et `ProgressBar` (propriétaire `internal/app/view.go`,

281	  balayage : un appel à `tea.NewProgressBar` ou un littéral `tea.ProgressBar{` hors de

288	
289	Fichier : nouveau `internal/app/terminal_progress_program_test.go`. Il réutilise `runRouter`,

336	
337	- `Failed` vaut 0 sans échec. Avec 2 échecs dans le contexte et 1 dans un autre, il vaut 2 ;

347	
348	Fichiers :
349

357	- `.claude/CLAUDE.md` : dans la ligne `app-shell.md` du tableau, ajouter « the tab progress
358	  bar (OSC 9;4, `terminalProgress`) ».
359	- `docs-site/docs/explanation/app-shell.md` (techwriter) : un paragraphe utilisateur sur
360	  l'onglet et l'en-tête `Failed` de `:jobs`.
361	- `docs/backlog.md` : consigner la décision (périmètre, acquittement, agrégation) sous le
362	  prochain numéro D (archivist). Aucun ADR séparé : la décision est réversible et locale.

365	
366	- Windows Terminal : indéterminé, 0 %, 50 %, rouge plein, jaune plein ; retour à rien en fin

375	go test ./internal/jobs -run 'Summarize|Progress|FailureSeq|FailuresIn|LatestFailureSeq'
376	go test ./internal/app -run 'TerminalProgress|ProgressBar|OnlyTheRouter'

383	## Risques et points irréversibles
384	
385	- **Aucun point irréversible** : pas de format sur disque (la mémoire des échecs n'est jamais
386	  écrite) et pas de clé de configuration.

388	  pointeurs distincts.

# DEVDESK-211 : progression des jobs dans l'onglet du terminal (`View.ProgressBar`, OSC 9;4)

Statut : plan (architect). Sources lues : `docs/architecture/app-shell.md` (registre `internal/jobs`,
mémoire des échecs, diffusion `ChangedMsg`, fond du terminal), `docs/ux/bubbletea-v2-improvements.md`
§2.2 et §4, `.claude/plans/charm-v2-impact.md` §2 et §4 (F3), `internal/app/view.go`,
`internal/app/jobs.go`, `internal/jobs/{jobs,failure,registry,message}.go`,
`internal/ui/jobsview/{model,view,update}.go`, `internal/app/terminal_background{,_program}_test.go`,
et les sources de `charm.land/bubbletea/v2@v2.1.1` (`tea.go`, `cursed_renderer.go`) et
`x/ansi@v0.11.9/progress.go`.

## Questions bloquantes

L'étape 1 peut démarrer sans les réponses : la fonction pure reçoit des données déjà
filtrées par le routeur. Les réponses changent les étapes 2 et 4.

1. **Périmètre : quels runs et quels échecs alimentent la barre ?**
   - A. Ceux du contexte courant (`ChangedMsg.Context`), comme `:jobs` (D8).
   - B. Tous les contextes : la barre parle du processus.
   - **Recommandation : A.** Le critère 7 impose un équivalent textuel, et `:jobs` ne montre
     que le contexte courant. Avec B, la barre serait rouge à cause d'un échec que `:jobs`
     ne montre pas, et l'acquittement porterait sur ce que l'utilisateur ne voit pas.
     Coût de A : un scan lancé dans le contexte A n'apparaît plus dans l'onglet après un
     passage au contexte B.
2. **Acquittement d'un échec (« jusqu'à acquittement dans `:jobs` »).** La notion de
   « lu » n'existe pas aujourd'hui. Un échec ne disparaît que par un `done`, une nouvelle
   tentative ou un `Forget`.
   - A. Afficher `:jobs` à l'écran vaut lecture. On l'acquitte à l'entrée, puis en continu
     tant que la vue reste affichée.
   - B. Une touche explicite dans `:jobs`. Seules `Q` et `Z` sont libres (Rule 111), ce qui
     ajoute un verbe au vocabulaire.
   - **Recommandation : A.** Aucune touche ni règle nouvelle, et c'est le sens de la fiche UX.
3. **Avertissement (« suspendus ou annulés »).** Le registre n'a **pas** d'état « suspendu » :
   un blur ne suspend aucun job (app-shell.md, DEVDESK-210). Il ne reste que l'annulation.
   - A. Avertissement tant qu'un run annulé n'est pas soldé : l'arrêt est demandé et le
     travail en vol est attendu (sync, clone, file en cours de vidage). Une fois soldé :
     `nil`.
   - B. A, plus les runs annulés soldés jusqu'à leur acquittement, comme pour les échecs.
   - **Recommandation : A.** L'utilisateur a lui-même demandé l'annulation (`K` dans `:jobs`,
     `esc` dans l'explorateur). Un jaune persistant après coup serait du bruit. Si une
     suspension apparaît un jour dans le registre, elle se branchera ici.

## Faits techniques établis (Bubble Tea v2.1.1)

- `tea.View.ProgressBar *tea.ProgressBar` porte `{State, Value}`. Les états sont `None`,
  `Default` (valeur 0 à 100), `Error`, `Indeterminate` et `Warning`. `tea.NewProgressBar`
  borne la valeur à [0, 100].
- Le renderer n'écrit OSC 9;4 que lorsque la valeur change. Il compare `*last != *view` **par
  valeur à travers le pointeur gardé**. **Piège :** muter en place un `*tea.ProgressBar` déjà
  rendu rend le changement invisible. `View()` doit donc fournir un pointeur neuf à chaque
  appel, ce que garantit une fonction pure qui fabrique la valeur.
- Premier rendu avec `nil` : rien n'est écrit. Passage de non-nil à nil : `ESC ]9;4;0 BEL`
  (`ansi.ResetProgressBar`).
- `close()` (sortie, panique récupérée, `ExecProcess`) écrit la remise à zéro si la dernière
  vue avait une barre. `start()` (retour d'un `ExecProcess`) la réémet. **Le critère 1 « à la
  sortie » est donc tenu par le framework**, et on l'épingle par un test sur les octets
  (étape 3).
- Il n'existe ni requête de capacité OSC 9;4, ni détection dans Bubble Tea : la séquence part
  vers tout terminal. Un parseur ECMA-48 consomme une chaîne OSC jusqu'à BEL ou ST sans
  l'imprimer. DevDesk envoie déjà OSC 11 et 111 ainsi que le mode 1004. Le cas réel « tmux
  sans passthrough » reste à vérifier à la main (étape 5).

## Le total d'un lot est-il connu ? Oui : tout est livrable d'un coup

`Run.Total()` et `Run.Done()` existent. `Done` compte les items soldés : done, skipped et
failed. Un run ouvert (`NewOpenRun`, le clone pendant le parcours) n'a pas de total tant
qu'il n'est pas scellé (`Seal`). Ensuite, il en a un. Le pourcentage est donc calculable
sans toucher au registre. Le découpage en étapes permet malgré tout de livrer d'abord
l'indéterminé, l'erreur et l'avertissement (étapes 1 et 2), puis de vérifier le pourcentage
sur Windows Terminal (étape 5).

## Règles d'agrégation (à tester et à documenter)

Entrée : les runs **non soldés** du périmètre et les échecs du périmètre. Précédence, de la
plus forte à la plus faible (même ordre que la Rule 128 : error, warning, status) :

| # | Condition | `jobs.Progress.State` | `tea.ProgressBar` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ≥1 échec avec `Seq > readThrough` (non lu) | `ProgressError` | `{Error, 100}` |
| 2 | ≥1 run non soldé avec `Cancelled()` | `ProgressWarning` | `{Warning, Percent}` si mesuré, sinon `{Warning, 100}` |
| 3 | ≥1 run non soldé, tous mesurés | `ProgressPercent` | `{Default, Percent}` |
| 4 | ≥1 run non soldé, au moins un non mesuré | `ProgressIndeterminate` | `{Indeterminate, 0}` |
| 5 | sinon | `ProgressIdle` | `nil` |

- **Run mesuré** : `!run.Open() && run.Total() >= 2`. *Hypothèse :* un run à une cible
  (scan d'un élément, create, delete, index, pull unitaire) n'a pas de progression utile :
  il resterait à 0 % puis disparaîtrait. Il compte donc comme indéterminé.
- **Pourcentage** : `floor(100 × Σ Done / Σ Total)` sur les runs non soldés, c'est-à-dire
  une somme pondérée et non la moyenne des pourcentages. Exemple : 1/2 et 0/8 donnent 10 %,
  pas 25 %. Le résultat est borné à [0, 100]. Un run seulement en file vaut 0 %.
- **Mixte** : un seul run non mesuré rend l'ensemble indéterminé (hypothèse du brief).
- **Un échec non lu domine tout**, y compris un registre vide (critère 4). Il disparaît
  aussi sans acquittement lorsque l'échec est effacé (nouvelle tentative réussie, `Forget`).
- *Hypothèse :* les valeurs 100 pour `Error` et pour `Warning` non mesuré donnent une barre
  pleine et visible sur Windows Terminal. À vérifier à la main (étape 5).
- *Hypothèse :* les échecs du kind `index` (parcours de la forge à l'ouverture de session)
  comptent, car `:jobs` les montre. Hors ligne, l'onglet passera au rouge jusqu'à la visite
  de `:jobs`. Choix ouvert, signalé dans la doc.

### Étape 1 : domaine (`internal/jobs`), numéro d'échec et fonction pure d'agrégation

Interfaces :

```go
// failure.go: Failure gains a registry-assigned, strictly increasing number.
type Failure struct {
	FailureKey
	Display string
	Detail  string
	At      time.Time
	// Seq orders failures for acknowledgement. Assigned by Registry.pose, never
	// reused, strictly greater on every pose (a re-posed key gets a new Seq).
	Seq uint64
}

// LatestFailureSeq returns the highest Seq in failures, 0 when empty.
func LatestFailureSeq(failures []Failure) uint64

// FailuresIn keeps the failures filed under contextName (D8, like FilterContext).
func FailuresIn(failures []Failure, contextName string) []Failure

// registry.go: Registry gains `failureSeq uint64`; pose sets f.Seq = ++r.failureSeq.

// progress.go
type ProgressState int

const (
	ProgressIdle ProgressState = iota
	ProgressIndeterminate
	ProgressPercent
	ProgressWarning
	ProgressError
)

// Progress is the whole registry summarized for one reader: the terminal tab
// (router) and the :jobs footer read the same computation.
type Progress struct {
	State    ProgressState
	Percent  int  // 0..100, meaningful when Measured
	Measured bool // every unfinished run is sealed with >= 2 targets
	Running  int  // unfinished runs
	Stopping int  // unfinished runs asked to stop (Run.Cancelled)
	Unread   int  // failures with Seq > readThrough
}

// Summarize applies the precedence table. runs and failures are already scoped
// by the caller (FilterContext / FailuresIn); it never filters by context.
func Summarize(runs []Run, failures []Failure, readThrough uint64) Progress
```

Pourquoi `Seq` et non `At` : deux échecs peuvent porter le même horodatage (résolution de
l'horloge, `SetClock` en test). Un filigrane fondé sur le temps en perdrait un.

Tests à écrire d'abord (tables, `progress_test.go`). Construire les runs avec `jobs.New()`
puis `Start`, `Advance`, `Cancel`, `Seal` et `Snapshot()`, ou par champs dans le package :

| Entrée | Attendu |
|---|---|
| `nil, nil, 0` | `Progress{}` (Idle) |
| un run soldé `done` | Idle (critère 6) |
| run ouvert non scellé, 0 cible | Indeterminate, Running 1 |
| `NewImmediateRun` (1 cible, running) | Indeterminate (hypothèse 1 cible) |
| scellé 4 cibles : 1 done, 1 failed, 2 queued, échec déjà lu | Percent 50, Measured |
| 1/2 et 0/8 | Percent 10, pas 25 |
| 1/3 | Percent 33 (arrondi par défaut) |
| 3 cibles toutes queued | Percent 0, State Percent |
| mesuré et ouvert ensemble | Indeterminate |
| sync annulé, un item encore running | Warning, Stopping 1 ; Percent conservé si mesuré |
| run annulé soldé | Idle |
| échec `Seq 3`, readThrough 2 | Error, Unread 1 |
| échec `Seq 3`, readThrough 3 | pas Error |
| échec non lu et run running | Error (précédence) |
| échec non lu et run en arrêt | Error |
| aucun run, échec non lu | Error (critère 4) |

Registre (`registry_failure_test.go`) :

- chaque `pose` attribue un `Seq` strictement croissant ;
- un échec reposé sur la même clé reçoit un `Seq` plus grand que l'ancien ;
- `Failures()` transporte `Seq` ;
- après l'éviction au-delà de `MaxFailures`, aucun `Seq` n'est réutilisé ;
- `LatestFailureSeq(nil) == 0`, puis le maximum ;
- `FailuresIn` ne garde que le contexte demandé.

Les littéraux `jobs.Failure{…}` existants des tests sont à champs nommés : ils compilent tels
quels, et aucune comparaison de struct entière n'a été trouvée.

Interfaces :

```go
// terminal_progress.go

// terminalProgress maps the summary to the tab's progress bar. Pure; returns a
// fresh pointer on every call (the renderer compares through the pointer it
// kept, so an in-place mutation would never be redrawn). nil when Idle.
func terminalProgress(p jobs.Progress) *tea.ProgressBar

// summarizeJobs scopes the snapshot to msg.Context, acknowledges what :jobs
// shows when it is on screen, and stores the summary. Called from Update only.
func (a *App) summarizeJobs(msg jobs.ChangedMsg)

// syncTerminalProgress is the level check run after every Update: it
// re-summarizes when the context changed since the last summary, or when :jobs
// is on screen with an unread failure (entry by any path: switchView,
// returnToOrigin, ...). Otherwise it does nothing (no snapshot copy per tick).
func (a *App) syncTerminalProgress()
```

Champs d'`App` :

```go
progress            jobs.Progress     // last summary; read by View()
progressContext     string            // context the summary was computed for
failuresReadThrough map[string]uint64 // acknowledgement watermark per context
```

Un filigrane par contexte : avec un seul filigrane global, acquitter dans B marquerait comme
lus les échecs de A de `Seq` inférieur, jamais vus. Avec la réponse B à la question 1, un
filigrane unique suffit.

Câblage :

- `broadcastJobs` : `msg := a.changedMsg()` puis `a.summarizeJobs(msg)` avant la boucle. Le
  calcul part bien du snapshot `ChangedMsg` (critère 7). Toute écriture du registre passe par
  `jobsChanged`, donc par `broadcastJobs`.
- `summarizeJobs` : `runs := jobs.Unfinished(jobs.FilterContext(msg.Runs, msg.Context))` et
  `fails := jobs.FailuresIn(msg.Failures, msg.Context)`. Si
  `a.currentView == command.ViewJobs`, le filigrane du contexte passe à
  `LatestFailureSeq(fails)`. Ensuite `a.progress = jobs.Summarize(runs, fails, readThrough)`
  et `a.progressContext = msg.Context`.
- `App.Update` (wrapper) : `model, cmd := a.update(msg)`, puis `a.syncTerminalProgress()`,
  puis `ensureTick` comme aujourd'hui.
- `view.go` : `v.ProgressBar = terminalProgress(a.progress)`. C'est la seule affectation du
  dépôt, et `View()` reste sans effet de bord.
- Le blur ne touche pas la barre : l'onglet sert justement quand DevDesk n'a pas le focus.

- mapping en table : Idle donne nil ; Indeterminate donne `{Indeterminate, 0}` ; Percent 42

- deux appels donnent deux pointeurs distincts, et muter le premier ne change pas le second ;
- routeur sans job : `a.View().ProgressBar == nil` (critère 1) ;
- `jobs.StartMsg` d'un scan de 4 cibles depuis `:sec` : `{Default, 0}`. Avancer 2 items
