1	# DEVDESK-211 : progression des jobs dans l'onglet du terminal (`View.ProgressBar`, OSC 9;4)
2	
3	Statut : plan (architect). Sources lues : `docs/architecture/app-shell.md` (registre `internal/jobs`,
4	mémoire des échecs, diffusion `ChangedMsg`, fond du terminal), `docs/ux/bubbletea-v2-improvements.md`
5	§2.2 et §4, `.claude/plans/charm-v2-impact.md` §2 et §4 (F3), `internal/app/view.go`,
6	`internal/app/jobs.go`, `internal/jobs/{jobs,failure,registry,message}.go`,
7	`internal/ui/jobsview/{model,view,update}.go`, `internal/app/terminal_background{,_program}_test.go`,
8	et les sources de `charm.land/bubbletea/v2@v2.1.1` (`tea.go`, `cursed_renderer.go`) et
9	`x/ansi@v0.11.9/progress.go`.
10	
11	## Questions bloquantes
12	
13	L'étape 1 peut démarrer sans les réponses : la fonction pure reçoit des données déjà
14	filtrées par le routeur. Les réponses changent les étapes 2 et 4.
15	
16	1. **Périmètre : quels runs et quels échecs alimentent la barre ?**
17	   - A. Ceux du contexte courant (`ChangedMsg.Context`), comme `:jobs` (D8).
18	   - B. Tous les contextes : la barre parle du processus.
19	   - **Recommandation : A.** Le critère 7 impose un équivalent textuel, et `:jobs` ne montre
20	     que le contexte courant. Avec B, la barre serait rouge à cause d'un échec que `:jobs`
21	     ne montre pas, et l'acquittement porterait sur ce que l'utilisateur ne voit pas.
22	     Coût de A : un scan lancé dans le contexte A n'apparaît plus dans l'onglet après un
23	     passage au contexte B.
24	2. **Acquittement d'un échec (« jusqu'à acquittement dans `:jobs` »).** La notion de
25	   « lu » n'existe pas aujourd'hui. Un échec ne disparaît que par un `done`, une nouvelle
26	   tentative ou un `Forget`.
27	   - A. Afficher `:jobs` à l'écran vaut lecture. On l'acquitte à l'entrée, puis en continu
28	     tant que la vue reste affichée.
29	   - B. Une touche explicite dans `:jobs`. Seules `Q` et `Z` sont libres (Rule 111), ce qui
30	     ajoute un verbe au vocabulaire.
31	   - **Recommandation : A.** Aucune touche ni règle nouvelle, et c'est le sens de la fiche UX.
32	3. **Avertissement (« suspendus ou annulés »).** Le registre n'a **pas** d'état « suspendu » :
33	   un blur ne suspend aucun job (app-shell.md, DEVDESK-210). Il ne reste que l'annulation.
34	   - A. Avertissement tant qu'un run annulé n'est pas soldé : l'arrêt est demandé et le
35	     travail en vol est attendu (sync, clone, file en cours de vidage). Une fois soldé :
36	     `nil`.
37	   - B. A, plus les runs annulés soldés jusqu'à leur acquittement, comme pour les échecs.
38	   - **Recommandation : A.** L'utilisateur a lui-même demandé l'annulation (`K` dans `:jobs`,
39	     `esc` dans l'explorateur). Un jaune persistant après coup serait du bruit. Si une
40	     suspension apparaît un jour dans le registre, elle se branchera ici.
41	
42	## Faits techniques établis (Bubble Tea v2.1.1)
43	
44	- `tea.View.ProgressBar *tea.ProgressBar` porte `{State, Value}`. Les états sont `None`,
45	  `Default` (valeur 0 à 100), `Error`, `Indeterminate` et `Warning`. `tea.NewProgressBar`
46	  borne la valeur à [0, 100].
47	- Le renderer n'écrit OSC 9;4 que lorsque la valeur change. Il compare `*last != *view` **par
48	  valeur à travers le pointeur gardé**. **Piège :** muter en place un `*tea.ProgressBar` déjà
49	  rendu rend le changement invisible. `View()` doit donc fournir un pointeur neuf à chaque
50	  appel, ce que garantit une fonction pure qui fabrique la valeur.
51	- Premier rendu avec `nil` : rien n'est écrit. Passage de non-nil à nil : `ESC ]9;4;0 BEL`
52	  (`ansi.ResetProgressBar`).
53	- `close()` (sortie, panique récupérée, `ExecProcess`) écrit la remise à zéro si la dernière
54	  vue avait une barre. `start()` (retour d'un `ExecProcess`) la réémet. **Le critère 1 « à la
55	  sortie » est donc tenu par le framework**, et on l'épingle par un test sur les octets
56	  (étape 3).
57	- Il n'existe ni requête de capacité OSC 9;4, ni détection dans Bubble Tea : la séquence part
58	  vers tout terminal. Un parseur ECMA-48 consomme une chaîne OSC jusqu'à BEL ou ST sans
59	  l'imprimer. DevDesk envoie déjà OSC 11 et 111 ainsi que le mode 1004. Le cas réel « tmux
60	  sans passthrough » reste à vérifier à la main (étape 5).
61	
62	## Le total d'un lot est-il connu ? Oui : tout est livrable d'un coup
63	
64	`Run.Total()` et `Run.Done()` existent. `Done` compte les items soldés : done, skipped et
65	failed. Un run ouvert (`NewOpenRun`, le clone pendant le parcours) n'a pas de total tant
66	qu'il n'est pas scellé (`Seal`). Ensuite, il en a un. Le pourcentage est donc calculable
67	sans toucher au registre. Le découpage en étapes permet malgré tout de livrer d'abord
68	l'indéterminé, l'erreur et l'avertissement (étapes 1 et 2), puis de vérifier le pourcentage
69	sur Windows Terminal (étape 5).
70	
71	## Règles d'agrégation (à tester et à documenter)
72	
73	Entrée : les runs **non soldés** du périmètre et les échecs du périmètre. Précédence, de la
74	plus forte à la plus faible (même ordre que la Rule 128 : error, warning, status) :
75	
76	| # | Condition | `jobs.Progress.State` | `tea.ProgressBar` |
77	|---|---|---|---|
78	| 1 | ≥1 échec avec `Seq > readThrough` (non lu) | `ProgressError` | `{Error, 100}` |
79	| 2 | ≥1 run non soldé avec `Cancelled()` | `ProgressWarning` | `{Warning, Percent}` si mesuré, sinon `{Warning, 100}` |
80	| 3 | ≥1 run non soldé, tous mesurés | `ProgressPercent` | `{Default, Percent}` |
81	| 4 | ≥1 run non soldé, au moins un non mesuré | `ProgressIndeterminate` | `{Indeterminate, 0}` |
82	| 5 | sinon | `ProgressIdle` | `nil` |
83	
84	- **Run mesuré** : `!run.Open() && run.Total() >= 2`. *Hypothèse :* un run à une cible
85	  (scan d'un élément, create, delete, index, pull unitaire) n'a pas de progression utile :
86	  il resterait à 0 % puis disparaîtrait. Il compte donc comme indéterminé.
87	- **Pourcentage** : `floor(100 × Σ Done / Σ Total)` sur les runs non soldés, c'est-à-dire
88	  une somme pondérée et non la moyenne des pourcentages. Exemple : 1/2 et 0/8 donnent 10 %,
89	  pas 25 %. Le résultat est borné à [0, 100]. Un run seulement en file vaut 0 %.
90	- **Mixte** : un seul run non mesuré rend l'ensemble indéterminé (hypothèse du brief).
91	- **Un échec non lu domine tout**, y compris un registre vide (critère 4). Il disparaît
92	  aussi sans acquittement lorsque l'échec est effacé (nouvelle tentative réussie, `Forget`).
93	- *Hypothèse :* les valeurs 100 pour `Error` et pour `Warning` non mesuré donnent une barre
94	  pleine et visible sur Windows Terminal. À vérifier à la main (étape 5).
95	- *Hypothèse :* les échecs du kind `index` (parcours de la forge à l'ouverture de session)
96	  comptent, car `:jobs` les montre. Hors ligne, l'onglet passera au rouge jusqu'à la visite
97	  de `:jobs`. Choix ouvert, signalé dans la doc.
98	
99	## Étapes
100	
101	Dépendances : 1, puis 2, puis 3. L'étape 4 ne dépend que de la 1 et peut se mener en
102	parallèle des étapes 2 et 3. L'étape 5 vient en dernier.

107	`internal/jobs/progress.go`, nouveau `internal/jobs/progress_test.go`, et
108	`internal/jobs/registry_failure_test.go` (ajouts).

120		// reused, strictly greater on every pose (a re-posed key gets a new Seq).
121		Seq uint64
122	}
123	
124	// LatestFailureSeq returns the highest Seq in failures, 0 when empty.
125	func LatestFailureSeq(failures []Failure) uint64
126	
127	// FailuresIn keeps the failures filed under contextName (D8, like FilterContext).
128	func FailuresIn(failures []Failure, contextName string) []Failure
129

131	
132	// progress.go

136		ProgressIdle ProgressState = iota

5		"strings"
6	
7		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/jobs"
8		sharedcomponents "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/help"

13		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
14	
15		tea "charm.land/bubbletea/v2"
16	)
17	
18	// GetTitle names the view, and the run when one is open.
19	func (m Model) GetTitle() string {
20		base := theme.IconHourglass + " Jobs"
21		if run, ok := m.openedRun(); ok && m.level == levelItems {
22			return base + " " + theme.IconChevronRight + " " + run.Label
23		}
24		return base
25	}
26	
27	// GetIcon returns the view icon. The title carries it, as everywhere else.
28	func (m Model) GetIcon() string { return "" }
29	
30	// GetHeaderInfo says how much of the session is on screen.
31	//
32	// Running first, because it is why the view is open. The total is the runs of
33	// this context, which is what the table holds — not the registry's, which also
34	// counts the ones a context switch is hiding.
35	func (m Model) GetHeaderInfo(_ string) []shortcut.HeaderInfo {
36		runs := m.visibleRuns()
37		return []shortcut.HeaderInfo{
38			{Key: "Running", Value: strconv.Itoa(len(jobs.Unfinished(runs))), Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle},
39			{Key: "Runs", Value: strconv.Itoa(len(runs)), Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle},
40		}
41	}
42	
43	// GetShortcuts returns the header's shortcut column (Rules 130, 137, 138).
44	//
45	// The obvious keys are absent: ↑↓, PageUp/PageDown, Home/End. What is left is
46	// the drill, the sort, the filter and help — and the three that vary are greyed
47	// rather than dropped, so the column is the same four lines at both levels.
48	func (m Model) GetShortcuts() shortcut.Shortcuts {
49		a := m.availability()
50		return []shortcut.Shortcut{
51			{Key: keymap.Kill, Description: "Stop", Disabled: !a.Stop.Enabled()},
52			{Key: "→", Description: "Open targets", Disabled: !a.Open.Enabled()},
53			{Key: "esc", Description: "Go back", Disabled: !a.Close.Enabled()},
54			{Key: ".", Description: "Sort", Disabled: !a.Sort.Enabled()},
55			{Key: "/", Description: "Filter"},
56			{Key: "?", Description: "Help"},
57		}
58	}
59	
60	// GetFooterHeight budgets the footer (Rules 124, 136).
61	//
62	// The breadcrumb is a line of the footer at the item level, and the filter bar
63	// adds its own when visible. Both are asked for here so the router can take
64	// them off the viewport.
65	func (m Model) GetFooterHeight() int {
66		height := 2 + m.filterBar().ExtraHeight()
67		if m.level == levelItems {
68			height++
69		}
70		return height
71	}
72	
73	// RenderFooter renders the lines below the viewport (Rule 124).
74	//
75	// Order: breadcrumb, filter bar, blank, message. The breadcrumb sits directly
76	// under the table because it names the level the table is showing (Rule 123).
77	func (m Model) RenderFooter(width int) string {
78		var parts []string
79		if m.level == levelItems {
80			parts = append(parts, m.renderBreadcrumb(width))
81		}
82		if bar := m.filterBar(); bar.IsVisible() {
83			parts = append(parts, bar.View())
84		}
85		parts = append(parts, theme.EmptyLineBg(width), m.footer.View(width, m.status()))
86		return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
87	}
88	
89	// renderBreadcrumb is the trail below the table at the item level (Rule 123).
90	// Breadcrumb mode: it is not navigable, the level shown is highlighted and the
91	// one above it is dimmed.
92	func (m Model) renderBreadcrumb(width int) string {
93		run, ok := m.openedRun()
94		if !ok {
95			return theme.EmptyLineBg(width)
96		}
97		tabs := []theme.TabItem{
98			{Label: "Runs"},
99			{Label: string(run.Kind) + " " + theme.IconChevronRight + " " + run.Label},
100		}
101		return theme.PadWithBg(theme.Bg(" ")+theme.RenderTabs(tabs, 1), width)
102	}
103	
104	// status is the derived line, with no timer (Rule 128).
105	//
106	// The text is the count, asked for with no origin: this view launched none of
107	// it, so the detailed form would be a lie about ownership. The detail is the
108	// selected row's own sentence (DescribeRun, or DescribeItem at the target
109	// level); while a row is selected its dot moves, so the footer spinner is
110	// dropped.
111	func (m Model) status() sharedcomponents.Status {
112		var st sharedcomponents.Status
113		if live := jobs.Unfinished(m.visibleRuns()); len(live) > 0 {
114			st.Text = sharedcomponents.Plural(len(live), "job", "jobs") + " running"
115		}
116		st.Detail = m.selectedDetail()
117		st.Spinner = st.Text != "" && st.Detail.IsZero()
118		return st
119	}
120	
121	// selectedDetail is the sentence of the row under the cursor, zero when there
122	// is none.
123	func (m Model) selectedDetail() sharedcomponents.RowDetail {
124		if m.level == levelItems {
125			run, ok := m.openedRun()
126			row, sel := m.itemTable.Selected()
127			if !ok || !sel {
128				return sharedcomponents.RowDetail{}
129			}
130			return sharedcomponents.DescribeItem(run.Kind, row.Item).Detail
131		}
132		if row, ok := m.runTable.Selected(); ok {
133			return sharedcomponents.DescribeRun(row.Run).Detail
134		}
135		return sharedcomponents.RowDetail{}
136	}
137	
138	// View is the Bubble Tea v2 face of Render: the content only. The terminal
139	// state (alternate screen, colours) belongs to whoever owns the program.
140	func (m Model) View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }
141	
142	// Render renders the table of the level on screen.
143	//
144	// There is no loading branch: this view fetches nothing, so it is never between
145	// a request and an answer. A table with nothing to show still renders its
146	// header and no rows (datatable.View() does this on its own) — the count that
147	// says why (zero runs, or a filter matching none of them) lives in the header
148	// (GetHeaderInfo), not in the body.
149	func (m Model) Render() string {
150		if m.level == levelItems {
151			return m.itemTable.View()
152		}
153		return m.runTable.View()
154	}
155	
156	// GetHelpContent returns the help for `?` (Rule 114).
157	func (m Model) GetHelpContent() help.Content {
158		return help.Content{
159			Title: "Jobs",
160			Description: "Everything long-running the application has started this session: scans, syncs, clones, image pulls and deletes. " +
161				"A run is one batch started in one go from one view; press → to see the targets it holds. " +
162				"This view starts nothing and owns nothing — it reads the same record every other view reads.",
163			KeyBindings: []help.KeyBinding{
164				{Key: keymap.Kill, Description: "Stop the selected run, or the selected target inside one"},
165				{Key: "→", Description: "Open the selected run and list its targets"},
166				{Key: "esc", Description: "Go back to the list of runs"},
167				{Key: ".", Description: "Cycle the sort column (runs only). Each press toggles asc/desc, then moves to the next column"},
168				{Key: "/", Description: "Filter by kind, state, label or target"},
169				{Key: "↑/↓", Description: "Move the selection"},
170				{Key: "ctrl+p", Description: "Open command mode"},
171				{Key: "?", Description: "Show this help"},
172			},
173			Sections: []help.Section{
174				{
175					Title: "Runs",
176					Body: "Activity (first, untitled): the run's state as a dot — see the legend below.\n" +
177						"Kind: what the run does — scan, sync, clone, pull, create, delete, index (the forge listing the explorer and its g read, refreshed when a session opens).\n" +
178						"Label: what the batch was launched on — the directory, the registry, the repository.\n" +
179						"Progress: targets settled over targets held. A target that was skipped or that failed has settled: progress reports on what is left to wait for, not on what succeeded.\n" +
180						"State: queued, running, done, failed or cancelled. A run is failed as soon as one of its targets is, and cancelled beats failed — a run stopped on purpose reads cancelled even though its targets failed because of it.\n" +
181						"Started: when the run was admitted, relative.",
182				},
183				{
184					Title: "Targets",
185					Body: "Activity (first, untitled): the target's state as a dot — see the legend below.\n" +
186						"Target: the repository path, the image reference, the group.\n" +
187						"State: queued and running are different things — queued is waiting for a worker, running is holding one. A batch of twelve on four workers is four running and eight queued.\n" +
188						"Detail: what the state alone cannot say — why a sync was skipped, that a scan failed. A dash means there was nothing to add.\n\n" +
189						"The order is the one the batch was dispatched in, and it does not change: sorting by state would move a row out from under the cursor every time one settled.",
190				},
191				indicator.Legend(indicator.JobsLegend...),
192				{
193					Title: "What is listed",
194					Body: "Runs of the current context only. A run is stamped with the context it started in and kept for the session, so switching context hides them rather than dropping them — switching back brings them back.\n\n" +
195						"The last 20 settled runs are kept. A run still going is never dropped, however many have settled.",
196				},
197				{
198					Title: "Stopping work",
199					Body: "'" + keymap.Kill + "' on a run stops its queue: nothing further starts, whatever the kind. Targets still waiting are marked skipped, and the ones already running report their own outcome when they get there — a run that was stopped reads 'cancelled' rather than 'done', which is the distinction the list exists to keep.\n\n" +
200						"'" + keymap.Kill + "' on a single target is offered only where cutting the work leaves nothing behind: a scan and an image pull can be cut, a clone cannot — a half-written repository on disk is worse than one that finished. A sync waits out the fetch in flight, and a delete is never cut at all.\n\n" +
201						"The key is greyed when there is nothing to stop, and pressing it then says why in the footer rather than doing nothing.",
202				},
203				{
204					Title: "Where the rows come from",
205					Body: "The router owns one record of what is running and hands every view a copy of it. That is why a scan started in the workspaces list shows up here, and why the security inventory marks a row that this view also lists — it is the same work, recorded once.\n\n" +
206						"Nothing on this screen is fetched, so there is nothing to refresh: the rows change when the work does.",
207				},
208			},
209		}
210	}

24	// This view fetches nothing and launches nothing, so every test here drives
25	// Update with the one message it lives on — jobs.ChangedMsg — and reads what
26	// the tables and the header say back.
27	
28	func TestMain(m *testing.M) {
29		log.SetOutput(io.Discard)
30		// Reading a Cmd runs it, and a refusal carries a three-second footer expiry
31		// (Rule 128). The test that asserts on that duration lives in the package
32		// that owns it.
33		sharedcomponents.FooterMsgDuration = time.Millisecond
34	
35		code := m.Run()
36	
37		log.SetOutput(os.Stderr)
38		os.Exit(code)
39	}
40	
41	// ── Fixtures ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
42	
43	// testContext is the name the router would have stamped. Nothing reads it from
44	// disk — the view is told, which is the point.
45	const testContext = "work"
46	
47	var startedAt = time.Date(2026, 8, 29, 9, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
48	
49	// run builds a snapshot run. The registry stamps ID and StartedAt when it
50	// admits one; here they are set by hand because no registry is involved.
51	func run(id jobs.JobID, kind jobs.Kind, label string, states ...jobs.ItemState) jobs.Run {
52		targets := make([]string, len(states))
53		for i := range states {
54			targets[i] = label + "/target" + string(rune('a'+i))
55		}
56		r := jobs.NewRun(kind, command.ViewWorkspaces, testContext, label, targets...)
57		for i, state := range states {
58			r.Items[i].State = state
59		}
60		r.ID = id
61		r.StartedAt = startedAt
62		return r
63	}
64	
65	func newModel(t *testing.T) Model {
66		t.Helper()
67		m := New(config.Default(), testContext)
68		m.resize(120, 20)
69		return m
70	}
71	
72	// feed sends one message and returns the settled model.
73	func feed(t *testing.T, m Model, msg tea.Msg) Model {
74		t.Helper()
75		updated, _ := m.Update(msg)
76		next, ok := updated.(Model)
77		if !ok {
78			t.Fatalf("Update returned %T, want jobsview.Model", updated)
79		}
80		return next
81	}
82	
83	func step(t *testing.T, m Model, msg tea.Msg) (Model, tea.Cmd) {
84		t.Helper()
85		updated, cmd := m.Update(msg)
86		next, ok := updated.(Model)
87		if !ok {
88			t.Fatalf("Update returned %T, want jobsview.Model", updated)
89		}
90		return next, cmd
91	}
92	
93	func withRuns(t *testing.T, runs ...jobs.Run) Model {
94		t.Helper()
95		m := feed(t, newModel(t), jobs.ChangedMsg{Runs: runs})
96		return feed(t, m, jobs.FrameMsg{Blink: true})
97	}
98	
99	// ── The snapshot is the only source ──────────────────────────────────────────
100	
101	func TestTheRowsComeFromTheSnapshot(t *testing.T) {
102		m := withRuns(t,
103			run(1, jobs.KindScan, "~/work", jobs.ItemDone, jobs.ItemRunning),
104			run(2, jobs.KindSync, "~/perso", jobs.ItemDone),
105		)
106	
107		if got := len(m.runTable.Items()); got != 2 {
108			t.Fatalf("the table holds %d runs, want the 2 in the snapshot", got)
109		}
110		view := m.Render()
111		for _, want := range []string{"~/work", "~/perso", "scan", "sync"} {
112			if !strings.Contains(view, want) {
113				t.Errorf("the table does not show %q:\n%s", want, view)
114			}
115		}
116	}

118	// D8: a run is stamped with the context it started in and kept for the session,
119	// so a context switch hides it rather than dropping it. The view filters.
120	func TestARunFromAnotherContextIsNotListed(t *testing.T) {
121		mine := run(1, jobs.KindScan, "~/work", jobs.ItemDone)
122		theirs := run(2, jobs.KindScan, "~/elsewhere", jobs.ItemDone)
123		theirs.Context = "another-context"
124	
125		m := withRuns(t, mine, theirs)
126	
127		if got := len(m.runTable.Items()); got != 1 {
128			t.Fatalf("the table holds %d runs, want only the current context's", got)
129		}
130		if strings.Contains(m.Render(), "~/elsewhere") {
131			t.Error("a run stamped with another context is on screen")
132		}

137	func TestRightOpensTheRunAndEscComesBack(t *testing.T) {

139

1	package jobsview
2	
3	import (
4		tea "charm.land/bubbletea/v2"
5	
6		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/jobs"
7		sharedcomponents "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
8		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/keymap"
9	)
10	
11	// Init returns nothing.
12	//
13	// The view fetches nothing and starts no chain: its rows arrive in the
14	// broadcast, and switchView hands it the snapshot on the way in (sendJobsTo).
15	// A view that asked on arrival would be reading a second answer to a question
16	// the router already holds.
17	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd { return nil }
18	
19	// Update handles messages.
20	func (m Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
21		switch msg := msg.(type) {
22		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
23			m.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
24			return m, nil
25	
26		case jobs.ChangedMsg:
27			return m.handleJobsChanged(msg)
28	
29		case jobs.FrameMsg:
30			return m.handleFrameMsg(msg)
31	
32		case tea.KeyPressMsg:
33			return m.handleKeyMsg(msg)
34	
35		case tea.PasteMsg:
36			return m.handlePaste(msg)
37		}
38	
39		m.footer.Handle(msg)
40		return m, nil
41	}
42	
43	// handleJobsChanged takes the router's snapshot and rebuilds both tables.
44	//
45	// Both, not just the one on screen: the item table is what the cursor stands in
46	// while a target settles under it, and rebuilding it only on the way in would
47	// freeze it at the moment it was opened.
48	func (m Model) handleJobsChanged(msg jobs.ChangedMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
49		m.runs = msg.Runs
50		m.refreshRows()
51		return m, nil
52	}
53	
54	// handleFrameMsg takes the animation's frame: the blink phase of both tables,
55	// which they read at render, and the footer spinner. No row is rebuilt.
56	func (m Model) handleFrameMsg(msg jobs.FrameMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
57		m.runTable.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)
58		m.itemTable.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)
59		m.footer.SetSpinnerFrame(msg.RenderedFrame)
60		return m, nil
61	}
62	
63	// visibleRuns is what this view shows: the runs of the current context (D8).
64	// The table decides the order; this decides which exist.
65	func (m Model) visibleRuns() []jobs.Run {
66		return jobs.FilterContext(m.runs, m.contextName)
67	}
68	
69	// openedRun returns the run the item level is showing, and whether it is still
70	// in the snapshot.
71	//
72	// It can stop being: the registry keeps the last MaxFinishedRuns settled runs,
73	// so a run left open long enough is eventually pruned out from under the
74	// cursor. refreshRows is what answers for that.
75	func (m Model) openedRun() (jobs.Run, bool) {
76		for _, run := range m.visibleRuns() {
77			if run.ID == m.openRun {
78				return run, true
79			}
80		}
81		return jobs.Run{}, false
82	}
83	
84	// refreshRows rebuilds both tables from the snapshot, and falls back to the
85	// list when the run being shown has been pruned.
86	func (m *Model) refreshRows() {

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X

5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.

       entire graph capabilities --json

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one animation tick (blink phase, `app.motion`), the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`, `ChangedMsg.Failures`), the activity-column guard (`activity_guard_test.go`), the terminal hand-off to child processes (the exec wrapper `internal/ui/teaexec`, use it instead of `tea.ExecProcess`, D121) and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci`, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface` |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage`, `internal/ui/datatable`, and the activity indicator column (`internal/ui/indicator`, `datatable.IndicatorColumn`, the row sentences `components.DescribeRow`) |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. # Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.

- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator

- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

</system-reminder>

# TUI — Forms & Focus

### Rule 103 : Standardized form navigation

- `↑ / ↓` to navigate between a form's fields
- A visual indicator (`theme.IconCircleSmall`) must show the focused element
- `Enter` to validate action buttons only (see Rule 135)

### Rule 104 : Modal window structure

- Rounded border (NormalBorder) with color appropriate to the context
- Title at the top using `theme.TitleStyle`
- Message in the center
- Buttons at the bottom with consistent spacing
- Help instructions with `theme.HelpStyle` at the very bottom
- Safe choice by default (e.g. "No" for delete confirmations)

**Palette variant (selector, Rule 112).** Border and title only: the title sits in
the top border, the border is `theme.ColorPaletteBorder`, there are no buttons and
no help line (Rule 134; the header lists the keys). Every line has an explicit
background and the exact width of the frame.

### Rule 113 : Form field spacing

| Layout | Separator after the field |
|--------|--------------------------|
| **Multi-line**: label ↵ content | `\n\n` (blank line) |
| **Single-line**: label + content on the same line | `\n` |
| **Checkboxes** | `\n` between them, `\n\n` after the group |

`renderField()` functions must **NOT** include the trailing separator.

### Rule 114 : Built-in help system (`?`)

**Every view implements `help.Provider` via `GetHelpContent()`, always in English.**

Obligations:
- Mandatory update in the same commit whenever a feature / keybinding changes
- Every new view must implement `help.Provider` with complete content

Expected content: `Title`, `Description`, `KeyBindings`, `Sections`

Files:
- `internal/ui/help/help.go` — component and `Provider` interface
- `internal/ui/*/view.go` or `model.go` — per-view implementation

**Declared gap: the command palette has no in-app help.** It is not a view; its
keys (`↑↓`, `tab`, `enter`, `esc`) are in the header while it is open and
documented in `docs-site/docs/reference/commands.md` (DEVDESK-89, decision of
the user).

### Rule 120 : Focus indicator and form field rendering

**Indentation: 2 characters.** When focused, `theme.IconCircleSmall` sits at column 0.

| State | Prefix |
|------|---------|
| Focused | `IconCircleSmall + " "` → `● Label` |
| Not focused | `"  "` (2 spaces) → `  Label` |

`theme.IconCircleSmall` (`\ueb8a`) does NOT contain a space — always add `" "` after it.

**Label/value separator**: `theme.IconChevronRight` (`\uf054`) + `" "`. **No `:`**.

**A space before the chevron is mandatory**: there must always be a space between the label text and `IconChevronRight`.

```go
// ✅ Single-line, focused
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Server " + theme.IconChevronRight + " ") + input.View()

// ✅ Multi-ligne
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name " + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
theme.Bg("  ") + input.View()

// ❌ WRONG — no space before the chevron
theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall + " Name" + theme.IconChevronRight) + "\n"
theme.KeyStyle.Render("▸ Server: ") + input.View()
```

**Selection lists**: `IconCircleSmall` for the selected item, `"  "` for the others.

**Focus color**: `theme.ColorHighlight` for all field types.

**TextInput cursor**: configure via `theme.StyleTextInput(&myInput)` (sets `Prompt = ""`).

**Checkboxes**: via `theme.RenderCheckbox()`.

**There are no radio buttons.** For a closed set of values, the control is
the `←→` cycle field (Rule 132) — regardless of how many values there are,
even two. `theme.RenderRadioButton()` was removed along with its last two
callers (§3.9 of the backlog); recreating it locally is forbidden.

Forbidden:
- ❌ `▸` as a focus indicator (use `theme.IconCircleSmall`)
- ❌ `:` as the label/value separator (use `theme.IconChevronRight`)
- ❌ `ColorPrimary` for focused elements (use `ColorHighlight`)
- ❌ Recreating `RenderCheckbox` locally
- ❌ Reintroducing radio buttons, in any form

### Rule 131 : Top padding for forms in the viewport

**Every form displayed in the main viewport must begin with exactly one blank line (1-line top padding).**

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — a single blank line
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n" +
        f.renderFields()
}

// ❌ WRONG — two blank lines (EmptyLineBg + "\n\n")
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(f.width) + "\n\n" + f.renderFields()
}

// ❌ WRONG — form stuck to the viewport's top edge
func (f *Form) View() string {
    return f.renderFields()
}
```

Does not apply to modals (positioned via `lipgloss.Place`).

### Rule 132 : Closed-list fields (value cycling)

**Any field whose value belongs to a finite set must use the ←→ cycle pattern.**

It is the **only** control allowed for a closed set. Radio buttons are not
an alternative for two or three values: they no longer exist in the
application (Rule 120). Checkboxes remain for independent booleans, which is
a different thing from an exclusive choice.

#### Visual

```
  Visibility  󰅂 private        ← not focused
● Visibility  󰅂 internal       ← focused (KeyStyle)
```

Line structure:

| Part | Value |
|--------|--------|
| Focus indicator | `theme.IconCircleSmall + " "` (focused) or `"  "` (not focused) |
| Label | field text, e.g. `"Visibility"` |
| Selection icon | `" " + theme.IconSelect + " "` |
| Separator | `theme.IconChevronRight + " "` |
| Current value | plain text with `ColorText` |

#### Navigation

- `←` / `→`: move to the previous / next value (cycling)
- `Tab` / `Shift+Tab`: navigate to the previous / next field

Do not use `Enter` to cycle — `Enter` confirms the form or advances to the next field.

#### Reference implementation

```go
// Rendu
func (f *Form) renderCycleField(label string, options []string, idx int, fieldIdx int) string {
    selectLabel := label + " " + theme.IconSelect + " "
    value := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorText).Render(options[idx])
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        return theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
    }
    return theme.Bg("  "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
}

// Key handling
case "left":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx - 1 + len(f.options)) % len(f.options)
    }
case "right":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx + 1) % len(f.options)
    }
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ Using `Enter` to cycle values
- ❌ Opening a dropdown list for 2–4 values (reserve that for long lists, cf. `renderTemplateList`)
- ❌ Hardcoding the value's color (use `ColorText`)
- ❌ Using radio buttons for a closed set (Rule 120)

### Rule 121 : Circular iconography for statuses

Status indicators in tables and lists must use circular icons:

| State | Icon |
|------|-------|
| Success / OK | `theme.IconOK` (`\uf058`) |
| Error / Failure | `theme.IconError` (`\uf057`) |
| Warning | `theme.IconWarning` (`\uf071`) |

Applies to: scan results, pipeline statuses, UP/DOWN indicators.
Does not apply to: object-type icons (folders, files, GitLab logo).

**Amendment (DEVDESK-137): the activity column is not covered.** In the activity
column (Rule 125, "The activity column"), the state is a glyph of
`internal/ui/indicator` (`● ○ ◴ ⊗ ◐ ◕ ◉ ⊘ ⊖ ◌`), colored by the closed
`theme.ColorActivity*` aliases, and not `IconOK` / `IconError` / `IconWarning`.
Every other status column (Verdict, Update, Sig, scan results, UP/DOWN) keeps
the three icons above, unchanged.

### Rule 133 : Multi-line text fields — `WrappedInput` mandatory

**`bubbles/textarea` is forbidden.** Its internal background is not controllable by lipgloss and produces visual artifacts (a `┃` gutter, terminal background between lines).

Use **`components.WrappedInput`** (`internal/ui/components/wrapped_input.go`) for any text field that must display across multiple lines.

#### API

```go
// Creation
field := components.NewWrappedInput(wrapWidth, charLimit, "placeholder text")

// Resizing — call inside the tea.WindowSizeMsg handler
field.SetDisplayWidth(terminalWidth)

// Focus / Blur
field.Focus()   // called from updateFocus()
field.Blur()    // called from updateFocus()

// Dans Update() — passer les messages clavier quand le champ a le focus
field, cmd = field.Update(msg)

// In View() — returns the multi-line content block, ready to concatenate
return labelStr + "\n" + field.View()

// Retrieving the value on submit
value := field.Value()
```

#### `wrapWidth` parameter

`wrapWidth` is the number of **runes** per visual line before wrapping (word-wrap at the last space, hard-break if there is no space).

| Context | Recommended value |
|----------|--------------------|
| GitLab description (group/project) | `80` |
| Short notes field | `60` |
| Long text field | `100` |

```go
// ✅ CORRECT
const descWrapWidth = 80
descInput := components.NewWrappedInput(descWrapWidth, 250, "description (optional)")

// ❌ WRONG
descInput := textarea.New()
```

#### Behavior

- Empty field + focused → only the block cursor is shown
- Empty field + not focused → placeholder in `ColorDim`
- Filled field → word-wrapped text, each line padded with `theme.PadWithBg` up to `displayWidth`
- Inverted block cursor (`ColorText` bg / `ColorBackground` fg) at the exact caret position

Forbidden:
- ❌ `bubbles/textarea` in any view
- ❌ Recreating the word-wrap or cursor logic locally
- ❌ Forgetting to call `SetDisplayWidth` in the `tea.WindowSizeMsg` handler

### Rule 135 : Strict keybinding assignment in forms ⚠️

**Every key has a single, unambiguous role.** These rules apply to every form in the application without exception.

| Key | Exclusive role |
|--------|---------------|
| `↑ / ↓` | Navigate between a form's fields |
| `Tab / Shift+Tab` | Switch between tabs **only** — never for navigation between fields |
| `Space` | Toggle a checkbox — the **only** key allowed for this role |
| `Enter` | Validate an action button or trigger a specific action — **never** to toggle a checkbox |
| `← / →` | Change level in a table (drill-down/up) **and** cycle the values of a closed-list field |
| `Esc` | Cancel / close / return to the parent level |

**Declared exception: the command line.** `tab` completes the highlighted
suggestion there (`keymap.DeclaredExceptions()`, surface `app/command-line`). The
command line has no tabs and no fields, so neither job of `tab` exists on it.

#### Detailed rules

**`Tab / Shift+Tab` — tabs only**
- Reserved for switching between tabs (`bubbles/table` breadcrumb, result tabs, etc.)
- Must **never** be used to move forward/backward between form fields
- If a view has no tabs, `Tab` must do nothing (or be ignored)

**`↑ / ↓` — navigation between fields**
- The only keys to move focus from one field to another in a form
- In a list/table outside a form: row-by-row movement (Rule 111)

**`Space` — toggle checkbox**
- The only valid key to check/uncheck a checkbox
- Match it as `keymap.Space`, never as a `" "` literal (Bubble Tea v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`; `keymap.Space` is `"space"`); `TestNoKeyIsComparedToALiteralSpace` fails on a literal
- Reference implementation: `LaunchForm` (`internal/ui/oci_resources`), pinned by `launch_form_keys_test.go` — `TestLaunchFormSpaceTogglesEachCheckbox`, `TestLaunchFormDetachAndInteractiveExcludeEachOther`, `TestLaunchFormEnterNeverTogglesACheckbox`
- `Enter` on a checkbox must be ignored or advance to the next field, never toggle it
- **Confirmation buttons are the mirror case**: `Space` never answers Yes or No. `components.ConfirmModal`, `ChoiceModal`, `OptionConfirmModal` and the setup wizard's confirmation answer on `enter` only (plus `y`/`n` on the yes/no ones). In `OptionConfirmModal`, `space` toggles the option checkbox when it has focus (inert when locked) and `enter` on that checkbox is ignored

**`Enter` — validation / action**
- Validates the currently focused button
- Triggers a contextual action (e.g. launch a scan, open a detail view)
- Must **not** toggle a checkbox

**`← / →` — table navigation and value cycling**
- In a table: `←` moves up a level (drill up), `→` moves down a level (drill down)
- On a closed-list field (cycle field): `←` previous value, `→` next value (Rule 132)
- Must **not** move focus between form fields

#### Common violations to avoid

```go
// ❌ WRONG — Tab to navigate between fields
case "tab":
    m.focusedField = (m.focusedField + 1) % fieldCount

// ❌ WRONG — Enter to toggle a checkbox
case "enter":
    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
    }

// ✅ CORRECT — Space to toggle
case keymap.Space:
    if m.focusedField == fieldMyCheckbox {
        m.myCheckbox = !m.myCheckbox
    }

// ✅ CORRECT — ↑/↓ to navigate between fields
case "up":
    m.focusedField = max(m.focusedField-1, 0)
case "down":
    m.focusedField = min(m.focusedField+1, fieldCount-1)
```

        return theme.KeyStyle.Render(theme.IconCircleSmall+" "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value

    return theme.Bg("  "+selectLabel+theme.IconChevronRight+" ") + value
}

// Key handling
case "left":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {
        f.idx = (f.idx - 1 + len(f.options)) % len(f.options)
    }
case "right":
    if f.focusedField == fieldIdx {

    }

# TUI — Theme, Colors & Background

### Rule 102 : Centralized management of colors and styles

- All colors must be defined in `internal/ui/theme/colors.go`
- Never hardcode colors directly in views
- Reusable styles must be defined in `internal/ui/theme/styles.go`
- Use the theme package's constants (ColorPrimary, ColorError, etc.)

### Rule 105 : Help message format

- Standard format: `[key] action  [key] action`
- Displayed with `theme.HelpStyle` (italic + ColorDim)
- Keys in square brackets `[]`
- Separated by at least 2 spaces

### Rule 115 : Uniform background handling (lipgloss)

**lipgloss does NOT propagate a parent's background to its children.**

`JoinHorizontal`/`JoinVertical` insert "bare" spaces that show the terminal's native background.

| Forbidden | Alternative |
|----------|-------------|
| `lipgloss.JoinHorizontal` to assemble blocks | Build each line manually with `PadWithBg()` |
| `lipgloss.JoinVertical` to stack lines | `strings.Join(lines, "\n")` with each line padded |
| `strings.Repeat("\n", n)` for blank lines | `theme.EmptyLineBg(width)` |
| `lipgloss.NewStyle().Render(text)` with no background | `.Background(ColorBackground)` mandatory |
| Hardcoded hex color | Global variables (`ColorBackground`, `ColorDim`, etc.) |

`JoinHorizontal`/`JoinVertical` are acceptable **only** if the result is wrapped in a `.Background(ColorBackground).Width(w)` style.

`lipgloss.Place` → always use `WithWhitespaceStyle(lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground))`
(Lip Gloss v2 removed `WithWhitespaceBackground`).

**Safety net, not a replacement (DEVDESK-209).** The router asks the terminal to
use `ColorBackground` as its default background (`tea.View.BackgroundColor`). The
helpers above stay mandatory: the native background is absent in 16-colour
terminals, under `NO_COLOR`, without a TTY, in a terminal or tmux that ignores
OSC 11, and during a `tea.ExecProcess` (the child sees the terminal's own
default). A bare cell there shows the user's background. See
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

**Known gap: the text input's cursor cell.** In Bubbles v2 the virtual cursor
(`textinput.Styles.Cursor`) carries a colour and no background, so that one cell
cannot take `ColorBackground`. `theme.StyleTextInput` sets every other state and
the cursor colour (`ColorHighlight`); the single-cell gap is accepted.

**Drawing over an already rendered screen** (the command palette) goes through
`overlay.Compose` (`internal/ui/overlay`) and nothing else: it splices with
`x/ansi` and never cuts an escape sequence. `lipgloss.Place` stays for full-screen
modals. Never slice a styled line by bytes or runes.

### Rule 117 : Centralized helpers of the `theme` package

**Never recreate `bg()`, `padWithBg()`, `bgWrap()` locally.**

| Function | Usage |
|----------|-------|
| `theme.Bg(s)` | Plain text with the app background |
| `theme.PadWithBg(content, width)` | Pad up to `width` with background |
| `theme.BgLine(s, width)` | Text + background + pad up to `width` |
| `theme.BgWrap(s, width)` | Background + pad on each line (multi-line) |
| `theme.EmptyLineBg(width)` | Blank line filled with background |
| `theme.OverlayBoxStyle()` | Standard style for overlay modals |
| `overlay.Compose(base, box, x, y, width)` | Box drawn over rendered lines, ANSI-safe |

- **Inline text** → `theme.Bg("text")`
- **Full line** → `theme.BgLine("text", width)`
- **Multi-line paragraph** → `theme.BgWrap(text, width)`
- **Blank line** → `theme.EmptyLineBg(width)`
- **Modal overlay** → `theme.OverlayBoxStyle().Render(content)`

### Rule 118 : Standardizing table and tab colors

| Element | Foreground | Background |
|---------|-----------|------------|
| Table header | `ColorSecondary` | — |
| Selected row (normal) | **each column's own** | `ColorTableLineSelected`, bold |
| Selected row (error) | `ColorBlack` | `ColorError` |
| Active tab | `ColorBlack` | `ColorSecondary` |
| Inactive tab | `ColorDim` | `ColorCommandLineBg` |

**Selected row (normal)** (§3.72 in the backlog; confirmed 2026-09-21). It used to
be one flat `ColorBlack` on `ColorSecondary`, dropping every column's own
colour — see Rule 122's "Selected row" section for why that used to be
mandatory and why it no longer is for this one variant: every cell now
repaints `ColorTableLineSelected` and bold **itself**, which is what makes
keeping the per-cell foreground safe instead of a return of the defect.
`error`, `busy` (`TableStylesForState`) and severity
(`TableStylesForSeverity`) are untouched — a solid background there still
means "this whole row is in that state," which per-cell colour would fight.

`ColorTableLineSelected` (`table_line_selected` in a theme file) is its own
key rather than an alias of `ColorSeverityLow`, on purpose: `ColorSeverityLow`
now points at the same tone as `ColorDim` — the colour the `:sec` inventory
already uses for a "0" count (Rule 122's "Color discipline") — so a theme
tuning "how muted is a LOW finding" no longer also retunes the selection
highlight by coincidence. Both keys default to the same hex the "normal"
selection has always used, so nothing changes on screen from this split by
itself.

Mandatory centralized functions:
- `theme.DefaultTableStyles()` — base style
- `theme.TableStylesForState(state)` — `"normal"` or `"error"`
- `theme.TableStylesForSeverity(severity)` — `"CRITICAL"`, `"HIGH"`, `"MEDIUM"`, `"LOW"`, `"UNKNOWN"`

Forbidden:
- ❌ Selection styles defined locally in views
- ❌ `ColorPrimary` for active tabs or headers (use `ColorSecondary`)

### Rule 119 : No hardcoded hex color outside `colors.go`

**A hex literal (`lipgloss.Color("#...")`, `color.RGBA{…}`) must appear ONLY in `internal/ui/theme/colors.go`.**

Palette variables are `color.Color` (`image/color`), not a Lip Gloss type. Read
one back with `theme.Hex(c)` (`#rrggbb`). A theme file is validated on load:
`theme.LoadTheme` refuses the whole file when a non-empty colour is not `#rgb`
or `#rrggbb` (see `docs/architecture/configuration.md`).

3-level architecture:

| Level | File | Role |
|--------|---------|------|
| **1. Base palette** | `colors.go` lines 6-32 | Raw hex colors (Catppuccin) |
| **2. Semantic colors** | `colors.go` lines 34+ | Aliases by usage, referencing the palette |
| **3. Styles** | `styles.go`, views | lipgloss styles using the semantic colors |

If a hex color is needed with no semantic equivalent:
1. Add it to the base palette (`colors.go`, hex section)
2. Create a semantic alias that references the palette

```go
// ✅ CORRECT
var ColorMaroon = lipgloss.Color("#eba0ac")  // in the base palette
ColorSeverityHigh = ColorMaroon              // in the semantic section

// ❌ WRONG
ColorSeverityHigh = lipgloss.Color("#eba0ac")  // hardcoded hex in the semantic section
```

`manager.go`'s fallbacks → reference `colors.go`, never hex values.

### Rule 127 : Relative time — `theme.TimeAgo`

**Every view displaying a relative time must use `theme.TimeAgo(t time.Time) string`** (`internal/ui/theme/timeago.go`).

| Duration | Output |
|-------|--------|
| < 1 min | `"now"` |
| < 1 hour | `"59 min ago"` |
| < 24 h | `"23 hr ago"` |
| < 30 days | `"30 days ago"` |
| < 12 months | `"11 mo ago"` |
| else | `"99 yr ago"` |
| zero | `""` |

Forbidden: local implementations, long formats, compact with no space.

### Rule 129 : Interface and log language — English US only

**All UI text and all logs must be in American English.**

| Category | Rule |
|-----------|-------|
| Labels, titles, UI messages | ✅ English US |
| Error messages (footer) | ✅ English US |
| Help (`GetHelpContent`, `GetShortcuts`) | ✅ English US |
| Cell values, empty messages | ✅ English US |
| Logs (`log.Printf`) | ✅ English US |
| Code comments | ✅ English only (Rule 307) |

```go
// ✅ CORRECT
theme.SpinnerMessage(m.spinner.View(), "Loading workspaces...")
m.footerError = "Failed to refresh — check logs"

// ❌ WRONG
theme.SpinnerMessage(m.spinner.View(), "Chargement des workspaces...")
m.footerError = "Échec du rafraîchissement — voir les logs"
```

| zero | `""` |

**All UI text and all logs must be in American English.**

| Help (`GetHelpContent`, `GetShortcuts`) | ✅ English US |

| Code comments | ✅ English only (Rule 307) |

// ❌ WRONG
theme.SpinnerMessage(m.spinner.View(), "Chargement des workspaces...")
